summary: Completed all 5 phases. Phase 1 replaced claude-refresh.sh's two-stage ps-aux-regex-then-ancestor-walk matcher with a single atomic ps -eo snapshot plus four named predicates (comm allow-list, /system.slice cgroup exclusion, invoking-UID ownership, inhibitor-target liveness), deleted the racing ancestor walk, added a main()/BASH_SOURCE guard, --dry-run, and a post-exclusion reclaim-memory accumulator. Phase 2 shipped scripts/tests/test-claude-refresh-matcher.sh (12/12 assertions, RED-proven against the pre-fix script at commit 7e79b2695) and registered it in manifest.json. Phase 3 made both timer ExecStart sites (claude-refresh.service and install-systemd-timer.sh) non-destructive by default (--dry-run instead of --force). Phase 4 reconciled skill-refresh/SKILL.md and commands/refresh.md with the real mechanism, forwarded --dry-run through Step 2, and recorded the non-destructive timer posture. Phase 5 swept all seven acceptance criteria read-only: live machine now reports 0 orphans (previously 10, all confirmed false positives, individually cross-checked against the new predicates); reclaim figure verified post-exclusion via a targeted fake-ps harness; --dry-run banner verified via a harness run with a synthetic orphan present; residual-claim grep, check-task-references.sh, and manifest jq checks all clean; no file written under .claude/**.
decisions_made: Unifying single-snapshot redesign chosen over patching the existing two-stage matcher, because the second live ps re-query is an inherent race that a walk-direction fix would not close.

is_claude_executable_comm's allow-list is exact-match on comm (claude, plus node gated by an argv entrypoint check), not a prefix/substring match -- this is what correctly excludes claude-memory-tracker (kernel-truncated comm 'claude-memory-t') without a bespoke exception.

Predicate 4 (inhibitor-target liveness) is retained and independently unit-tested even though comm-based matching already excludes today's observed inhibitors -- acceptance criterion 1(c) requires it, and it is the only predicate protecting OTHER live sessions rather than the invoker's own.
Timer ExecStart uses --dry-run rather than a bare no-flag invocation, so the non-destructive posture is visible in journalctl.

Recall is deliberately traded for safety: a missed orphan is preferable to killing a live daemon, and this trade-off is recorded in the script header so a future reader does not widen the match back toward argv.
The regression suite's mutation check is pinned to commit 7e79b2695 (the last commit before the Phase 1 rewrite), not HEAD, since HEAD at test-authoring time already is the fixed script.
dead_ends: A naive $PPID-based guess at 'the running script's own pid' inside the self-exclusion test harness's fake ps was wrong: snapshot=$(take_snapshot) forks an intermediate subshell to run that function, so the process that execs the fake ps is a grandchild, not a direct child, of the real script -- $PPID named the intermediate subshell. Fixed by walking real ancestry with the system ps and taking the highest ancestor whose argv still names the script under test.
